_comment: Curated chapter list for Lesson 1: ownership through pattern matching (Ch4 Understanding Ownership, Ch5 structs, Ch6 Enums and Pattern Matching). Deliberately small for the v0 proof-of-concept - extending this to the full milestone map is mechanical, not a redesign.
_relevanceThresholdRationale: Re-calibrated 2026-08-31 after the pack grew from 3 to 7 chapters (added slices, enums, match, if-let). The original 5.0, calibrated only against the 3-chapter ownership/structs corpus, broke down hard on the larger, more diverse one: an 8-good/7-bad probe (5 totally-off-topic or genuinely-uncovered-but-Rust-adjacent bad queries - traits, generics, Result/?, threads, plus 2 true off-topic controls) found 5 of 7 bad queries falsely grounded at 5.0, including 'how do I make a good pasta carbonara' scoring 6.55 - a pure cooking question, grounded purely because 'good' and stray phrasing overlapped the ownership chapter's vocabulary. Worse, this corpus does NOT admit any cleanly-separating scalar: the single worst false positive, 'how do I implement a custom trait for my struct' (traits are not covered by this pack at all), scored 12.90 - HIGHER than the best genuinely-good query in the probe (12.70, 'can I have multiple immutable references at once') - so no threshold can pass every good query while blocking it. Chose 9.0 as the best available trade-off: it eliminates 4 of the 5 confirmed false positives (pasta/threads/errors-Result/generics), at the cost of 3 of 8 good queries whose top score fell below it ('what does match do', 'if let vs match', 'struct vs tuple' - each phrased sparsely enough to score 6-8) now refusing and needing a rephrase. The 12.90 trait outlier remains a known, irreducible residual risk at any usable threshold - same class of BM25 corpus-heterogeneity limitation as content-packs/firmware/manifest.json's RAM-budget case, but here the overlap is total rather than a narrow band, so it could not be fully engineered away by threshold choice alone. See README's 'A real, honest limitation' section.
